newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ignore Matsushita news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ignore Matsushita news.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures traded sluggishly on Tuesday, ignoring news of a bad debt write-off by Matsushita Electric and comments by a Japanese official suggesting rates should rise.

"The Euroyen market is still very lethargic but I'm on the sell side, We've been stuck at these levels for the past three weeks and some of the weak longs have already bailed out," said a trader with a European institution.
He said players were likely to start setting up fresh short positions as the market had already priced in steady interest rates for another year.
Dealers said the market was unmoved by news Matsushita Electric Industrial Co would write off its 100 billion yen long-term loan to its troubled finance unit, NL Finance Co.

Comments by Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama that the interest rate gap between Japan and other countries should be narrowed also had little impact as players were unsure of their implications.
"The market didn't know how to react to Kajiyama," said the trader, noting that the JGB market had been very subdued with no large orders sighted.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.36 at 1118 GMT against its IMM close at 99.34 on volume of 5,720 lots. December was at 99.24 against 99.23 on 4,005 lots.
March JGBs settled at 126.17 against their previous 126.08.
Eurodollar futures were unmoved as players sat on their hands ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday.
"There's a little bit of selling pressure coming in. The trend is definitely downward but people won't do anything before Greenspan," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.
